key_insight: OrthoGen learns patient-specific outcome distributions over time under changing treatments by combining generative modeling with an orthogonal, doubly robust adjustment strategy.
clinical_relevance: This could improve risk estimation for individualized treatment sequences in settings where confounding changes over time, such as longitudinal care planning.
method: Introduces generative recursive g-computation to propagate full conditional outcome distributions instead of only means.
Builds generative learners for CDPO estimation using flexible backbones such as normalizing flows or diffusion models.
Adds OrthoGen, a Neyman-orthogonal, doubly robust learner designed to reduce sensitivity to nuisance estimation errors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong performance across synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world datasets, with OrthoGen described as highly effective.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate nuisance estimation and suitable generative-model training, so implementation quality and data shift remain important concerns.
paper_title: OrthoGen: A Generative Orthogonal Learner for Time-Varying Treatments
